title: Regional GPU surge buffer plan and slot matrix - Q2 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a pragmatic slot-based maintenance approach for GPU driver upgrades and planned hardware rotations across regions. Goal is to minimize customer impact while retaining an operational surge buffer for unexpected load. This is intentionally pragmatic: a mix of hard slots, soft reserves, and deterministic rollback triggers.

Scope:
- Applies to the public GPU fleet used for Hosted API + Dedicated in NA/EMEA/APAC regions.
- Covers software-level driver upgrades (NVIDIA driver releases and kernel ABI changes), minor host reboots, and controlled hardware swaps (node replacement).
- Excludes long-term capacity expansion (procurement) and single-host emergency repairs.

Key assumptions:
- Total fleet counts per region (rounded) are stable over the quarter.
- Normal steady-state utilization averages 62% across regions; peak 78% in NA evening window (PDT).
- We require a minimum 10% hard reserve for SLAs. Surge buffer is additional temporary capacity we prefer to keep free during maintenance execution.
- Significant client traffic patterns known and communicated (GTM + account teams will be notified for large customers).

Definitions:
- Slot: a fixed time and GPU-capacity reservation for maintenance on a subset of nodes.
- Hard reserve: capacity never drained for scheduled maintenance (SLA-backed).
- Surge buffer: temporarily available spare capacity we aim to preserve during major driver upgrades to absorb traffic spikes.
- Canary group: small set (~1%–3%) of hosts used to validate driver changes before broad rollout.

Regional slot matrix (baseline plan) - sample snapshot:
(Columns: Region | Total GPUs | Hard reserve (min) | Surge buffer target | Planned drain per maintenance day | Preferred maintenance window)

NA | 12,800 | 1280 (10%) | 640 (5%) | 1280 (10% of fleet) | Tue–Thu 02:00–06:00 PDT
EMEA | 8,400 | 840 (10%) | 420 (5%) | 840 (10% of fleet) | Wed–Fri 01:00–05:00 CEST
APAC | 6,200 | 620 (10%) | 310 (5%) | 620 (10% of fleet) | Mon–Thu 03:00–07:00 SGT

Notes: the planned drain per maintenance day is a soft target; we prefer staged 5–20% waves for large upgrades rather than one-shot 100% drains. Surge buffer target should be maintained until final validation checkpoint.

Driver upgrade cadence & execution pattern (recommended):
1) Pre-release staging: build and test driver on dedicated staging hosts; run internal smoke test suite (latency, kv-cache behavior, token-throughput).
2) Canary wave: pick 1% of hosts in each region (distributed by AZ) and apply driver + kernel changes. Run 4–12 hours of production traffic with verbose metrics. Successful canary => proceed.
3) Rapid-stagger rollout: apply changes in waves sized to 5–15% of remaining planned-drain capacity per 4–8 hour window depending on real-time telemetry.
4) Post-wave validation: 30–90 minute validation window with metric thresholds. If thresholds are violated, automated rollback for that wave only.

Stagger parameters (defaults):
- Wave size: 8% of region fleet (configurable by region).
- Pause between waves: 4 hours.
- Max concurrent drained capacity across regions: 18% total fleet (across all regions).

Telemetry and guardrails (automatic triggers):
- Abort & rollback if: p50 latency for generation endpoints increases >25% over baseline for 20 minutes; error rates >2x baseline for 10 minutes; queue depth growth shows >30% reduction in processing throughput.
- Throttle further waves if surge buffer drops below configured target (default 5% of total) or if specially-tagged enterprise customers report degraded behavior via monitoring channel.

Pre-drain checklist (to be completed and time-stamped in runbook):
- [ ] Confirm canary host pass status and signoff by release owner.
- [ ] Notify account-ops + CS for customers with >5% of their requests in affected region (>=24h notice).
- [ ] Reserve slot(s) in calendar and mark capacity in allocation sheet.
- [ ] Ensure automated fallback images are available (image id + sha).
- [ ] Snapshot KV cache metrics and flush plan documented.
- [ ] Confirm spare driver binary rollbacks staged in S3.

Evacuation & fallback options (fast-track):
1) Capacity swap into Dedicated overflow pool (if available) — redirect 10–15% of traffic for 30–90m using routing policy.
2) Route to compatible lower-memory model variants (quantized) as temporary fallback for latency-sensitive tiers.
3) Cross-region burst: failover small percentage of requests to nearest region if inter-region latency tolerable and customer's policy allows.

Communication plan (internal & external):
- Internal: #infra-maintenance Slack channel will be used for live execution updates. Page SRE on first sign of metric degradation per guardrails.
- External: Status page incident post if customer-visible degradation detected. Preplanned maintenance notices for customers in high-usage bands 24–72h prior.

Sample slot allocation CSV (for planners to paste into sheets) - columns: slot_id,region,drain_start_iso,drain_end_iso,estimated_gpus,owner,notes
slot-2026-05a,NA,2026-05-05T02:00:00-07:00,2026-05-05T06:00:00-07:00,1280,Aisha Patel,driver 535.86 canary + wave1
slot-2026-05b,EMEA,2026-05-06T01:00:00+02:00,2026-05-06T05:00:00+02:00,420,Marc Chen,stagger wave 1 - kernel minor patch
slot-2026-05c,APAC,2026-05-04T03:00:00+08:00,2026-05-04T07:00:00+08:00,310,Olivia Martinez,hardware swap - rack 12

Post-maintenance QA matrix (quick checks):
- Model correctness: sample prompts across 6 model families, check top-1 token divergence <0.7% vs pre-upgrade baseline.
- Latency: p50 within 10% of baseline, p95 within 20%.
- Throughput: throughput per GPU within +/-8% of baseline for typical batch sizes.
- Error rate: <0.5% absolute error increase.

Runbook excerpt — immediate rollback steps (if guardrail trips):
1) Halt rollout and mark wave as paused.
2) Re-launch fallback routing for affected customers.
3) Re-image hosts in the wave to previous image (automated script: infra/reimage/run-rollback.sh).
4) Re-run canary tests; do not resume broader rollout until explicit SRE + Release engineer signoff.

Operational notes and open questions (working):
- How many on-call SREs to commit for large cross-region upgrades? Suggest 2 primary + 1 escalation for NA/EMEA combined windows.
- Should we increase hard reserve to 12% for Q4 given projected holiday traffic? (Decision deferred to capacity planning meeting).
- Consider automated surge buffer booking tool that prevents scheduling when buffer dips below threshold — prototype task: JIRA-OPS-8499.

Appendix: quick references
- Canary checklist template: /confluence/gpu-canary-template
- Driver rollback image location: s3://redwood-infra/driver-rollbacks/2026-Q2
- Related playbooks: JIRA-OPS-8472 (driver upgrade playbook); github PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/gpu-drain-scripts#PR-231

Bottom line: this doc is intended to be used as a lightweight planning and execution guide for Q2 driver upgrades and scheduled GPU rotations. It favors staged waves, conservative surge buffer preservation, and automated guardrails to enable rapid rollback without impacting SLAs. Feedback welcome — please add comments inline and update slot CSV when you reserve time.
